summary: Iteration 1 confirmed two of three hypotheses and identified a concrete bug in the search algorithm: the 5-phase Pareto search found only 7 of 17 performance tiers (41%, vs. the 80% target) because it missed non-power-of-2 GPU counts (3, 5, 6, 7 GPUs) and incorrectly discarded high-preemption configs that are legitimately Pareto-optimal when KV cache cost is an objective. The KV cache saturation curve and GPU scaling trends were both confirmed with quantitative detail.
key_points: REFUTED — Tier coverage: Search found 7/17 tiers (41%) using 71 of 200 evaluations, well under budget but far short of the 80% threshold. Root cause 1: topology enumeration only covered 10 of 15 GPU configurations, skipping non-power-of-2 counts (tp=1 inst=3, tp=2 inst=3, etc.). Root cause 2: Phase 2 always minimized KV blocks toward zero-preemption, ignoring that high-preemption / low-kv_blocks configs (e.g., tp=1 inst=1 kv=2000 at 5.3 rps with ttft=20,695ms) are valid Pareto points when cache cost is an objective.

CONFIRMED — KV cache saturation: RPS rose monotonically from 11.31 → 19.56 as kv_blocks increased 2000 → 7500, then plateaued exactly at kv=7500 (where preemptions dropped to zero). TTFT_p99 fell 77% (11,442ms → 2,655ms). Saturation threshold is driven by effective token capacity (kv_blocks × block_size): both bs=16@kv=7500 and bs=32@kv=5000 converge to ~120k effective tokens at the threshold.

CONFIRMED — GPU scaling: Best RPS increases monotonically with GPU count (6.26 → 11.45 → 19.56 → 30.24 rps for 1/2/4/8 GPUs) and rps-per-GPU diminishes (6.26 → 5.72 → 4.89 → 3.78). Key nuance: the tp:inst ratio matters as much as raw GPU count — tp=8 inst=1 delivers 30.24 rps while tp=1 inst=8 delivers only 11.93 rps with the same 8 GPUs, because higher TP lowers per-token latency (ITL: 4.5ms vs 14.4ms).

Next iteration should fix the two identified search bugs: (1) expand topology enumeration to all 15 valid tp×inst combinations including non-power-of-2 GPU counts, and (2) retain preemption-regime configs as Pareto candidates rather than discarding them. Re-running the corrected search.py should bring tier coverage from 41% to ≥80% within the 200-evaluation budget.
